Module 3 of 15

LOS II — Credit data and decisioning

How a lender decides: the data it may use, the policy that judges it, and the humans and machines allowed to say yes.

Underwriting turns verified facts into a governed decision. This module covers the lawful data rails (credit bureaus and the Account Aggregator), credit policy as executable data, the deterministic decision engine, the human controls around referrals and overrides, and the guardrails on AI in credit.

4 lessons71 min guided timeComplete in sequence

Lesson 3.1 · 18 min

Credit data: bureaus (CICs) and the Account Aggregator

  • Explain what a bureau pull is, its permissible-purpose rule and what it returns
  • Describe the Account Aggregator consent artefact and data flow
  • Contrast bureau data with cash-flow data in underwriting

Lesson 3.2 · 20 min

Credit policy as data: eligibility and the decision engine

  • Explain FOIR and the standard eligibility knockouts
  • Describe why policy lives as versioned data, not code
  • State the decision engine's guarantees: deterministic, fail-closed, replayable

Lesson 3.3 · 15 min

Referrals, overrides and maker-checker

  • Treat 'refer' as a designed outcome with a governed resolution path
  • Explain override discipline: policy permission, independence, evidence
  • Describe the underwriter's workspace: CAM, conditions, sanction validity

Lesson 3.4 · 18 min

AI-assisted decisions: guardrails, human review and the kill switch

  • Explain how model outputs may lawfully influence a credit decision
  • Describe the kill switch and what 'degrade to human review' means
  • Summarise the governance around models and AI agents
